correctness.rationale: Even gamma makes all local blend weights positive; normalized nondecreasing data decompose into nonnegative step coefficients. Each negative step has one local extrapolation term. Its contribution is bounded by two positive weights; the exact scalar bound H(s) decreases for s>=1-t, giving delta_gamma. Reflection handles upper overshoot. With three sites the jump attains delta_gamma; any extra grid interval adds positive denominator weight and forces strict inequality at each nonnodal point, with compactness securing strict global nonattainment. Stationary equation has unique root because its two sides are strictly monotone. Real formulas checked against the source and exact rational finite tests; finite testing is supplementary.

value.rationale: A sharp three-knot defect alone offers no prediction for long-grid worst-case growth; proving it governs arbitrary n supplies a useful structural and size-uniform shape guarantee for a stable rational interpolatory family. The exact positivity contrast follows with an explicit sharp three-knot extremizer, while larger grids have strictly lower defects. This is mathematically motivated by the distinction between pole-free bounded Lebesgue stability and monotone data range control; it is not merely a known finite table computation.
